title: Smart Thermostat Rebates in Timmins 2026: $125 Back
desc: Timmins smart thermostat rebate for 2026: $125 from Home Renovation Savings, Hydro One as distributor, and the free Energy Affordability Program.
lead: Timmins has the coldest January in our 25 cities, an average low of -18.6°C, and 78% of its 17,890 households live in a house type the $125 rebate covers.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for a smart thermostat in Timmins
cards_intro: We re-read the three program pages on October 4, 2026. The rebate is province-wide, so the amount is the same in every city, and the page that matters is the one that says whether your home and heating qualify.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: One rebate on an eligible smart thermostat, claimed with a code at checkout or with a receipt uploaded within 60 days of buying.

cards.title: Who is eligible
cards.amount: Gas heat or electric heat or cooling
cards.note: You must be an Enbridge Gas customer heating mainly with a gas furnace or boiler, or be on the Ontario grid and use electric heat or cooling, and live in a house, semi, row, townhome or mobile home on a permanent foundation.

cards.title: One per household, ever
cards.note: A smart thermostat rebate, discount or free device from Enbridge, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings in the past rules you out.

cards.title: Peak Perks
cards.note: A prepaid card for joining the summer demand response program with central air or a heat pump controlled by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat.

cards.title: Energy Affordability Program
cards.note: Households under the income limits get a programmable or smart thermostat, depending on the home, with other upgrades at no charge.

cards.title: Cornwall excluded
cards.note: Cornwall Electric customers cannot join the rebate or Peak Perks.

after_cards: The rebate page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: Timmins averages -18.6°C in January and has recorded -39.3°C. Only 3% of its households live in tall buildings and 65% live in detached homes. The rebate's heating test is the thing to read closely, because it names gas, or electric heat or cooling, and says nothing about other fuels.

Hydro One is the distributor our lookup shows for Timmins. Hydro One serves a much wider area than the city utilities elsewhere on this list. Timmins postal codes begin with P, which the Energy Affordability Program lists, and the program says it is fully funded and accepting applications.

Before you buy, press the program page's Get code button, receive a code by email and enter it at checkout on the Home Depot, Best Buy, Copeland Sensi, ecobee or Mysa website. After you buy, press Apply for rebate and upload the receipt within 60 days. Either way the thermostat has to be one of the listed models, and a Timmins homeowner who buys in a store should keep the receipt.

Peak Perks pays a $75 virtual prepaid Mastercard when you enroll and $20 a year after. It needs central air conditioning, or a heat pump that is part of central air, run by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat from ecobee, Google Nest, Honeywell Home, Emerson, Trane or Alarm.com. On hot weekday afternoons the utility can adjust the setting by up to 2 degrees Celsius for no more than three hours, and you can opt out during an event. With the $125, a first year could bring in $200, though Peak Perks cannot be combined with other Ontario demand response programs.

The rebate page does not say owners only. It asks that you live in an eligible home type and that either gas or electric heating or cooling applies. In Timmins, 33% of households rent. A tenant should still get the landlord's agreement before replacing the thermostat on the wall and should ask whether it goes back when they leave.
claim_steps: Check that your home type, heating and cooling match the eligibility card, and that you have not had a thermostat offer before.
Pick one of the listed models from ecobee, Google Nest, Honeywell Home, Copeland Sensi, Mysa or Sinopé.
Get a code from the program page and use it at checkout, or buy first and upload the receipt within 60 days.
If you have central air, enroll the same thermostat in Peak Perks. Hydro One is your local distributor, but Peak Perks is run by Save on Energy.
If your household income is under the program limits, call 1-844-770-3148 before buying, since a free thermostat may be available.
faq: Does Hydro One offer its own thermostat rebate?
We did not find one on the pages we read.
Can I claim if I heat with propane?
The page does not mention propane. Ask the program, and check the Energy Affordability Program.
How do I apply for the free thermostat?
Phone 1-844-770-3148 or use the online form on the program page.
Is Timmins eligible for Peak Perks?
It is open to customers of any Ontario distributor with central air and an eligible thermostat.
